about: What real machines, and the people using them, showed must change in Windstorm Repo Minions, and the version each change is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_strand.py (class Promises) refuses a version while a row due in it has no test, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine.
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist and be named in the plan next to the codon.
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which kind of machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person the skill is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.seen: GitHub's documentation says a lock on an account can block GitHub Actions. A run that GitHub does not start ends 'startup_failure' with zero jobs, and no runner of the person's can change that. A test on another repository proves nothing about this one.
rows.promise: Before installing, look tests whether GitHub creates jobs for THIS repository and names a zero-job startup_failure as an account or repository matter; setup stops there and the skill is never offered as a way around it.
rows.moved_why: Moved to 0.1.1 by the maintainer's word, 2026-11-23, with the reason: the check is built and tested, but seeing it needs an account whose GitHub Actions start no jobs and the right to delete the repository made for it, neither of which this release had; the README's 'Not seen yet' part says so.

rows.seen: Seen: self-hosted runners attached to public repositories, guarded only by a same-repository condition in the workflow file and by approval of outside contributors. A fork's pull request runs its own copy of the workflow file, so the condition is not a boundary. Repositories also changed visibility after their runners were set up.
rows.promise: Refuse a repository that is not private, at the tool, and hold its runners within one watch interval when it stops being private.

Steered, the same steer as row R62: the watch's one privacy read was answered public by a wrapper put in front of gh (from 03:20:34Z to 03:29:27Z UTC, and three shorter times), everything else real: the watch's first pass held the runner and took it off the repository on GitHub's side once idle, status began with a stop saying every job is refused, a real job asking for our labels was refused, and `resume --private-again` then setup brought it back. Not seen: a repository really turned public with a runner on it, which is not done, by rule. Last checked 2026-11-24: the part not seen is taken by the maintainer's word (rule 32).
